title: From Servers to Racks
summary: See how racks organize many servers while supporting labeling, airflow, and connections.
objectives: Explain why data centers organize servers in racks.
Use labels and a simple diagram to show orderly equipment connections.

vocab.def: A frame that organizes equipment in a vertical arrangement.
A clear name or code that helps people identify something.
The movement of air through a space.

sections.heading: Organization helps people and systems
sections.body: A rack holds equipment in an orderly arrangement. Labels help people find the right server or cable, especially when many similar items are nearby.

sections.heading: Space affects cooling and connections
sections.body: Servers need planned airflow, and cables need routes that people can understand. Good organization makes it easier to observe, maintain, and explain a system.

sections.heading: Build a paper rack
sections.body: Draw a rack with six pretend server cards. Add labels and arrows for network connections and airflow. This classroom model is not a professional installation plan.

practice.prompt: A rack has 12 slots and 9 are occupied. How many slots remain? What information would a label add to your diagram?

quiz.question: Why are labels useful in a rack?
options: They help people identify equipment and connections
They allow anyone to bypass security
quiz.answer: They help people identify equipment and connections

reflectionPrompt: How did organization make your paper rack easier to understand?
